touches.text: Every part is its own process: the bus, each shim, each device, the ground loop. Any one can be stopped and restarted alone while the rest run on. WHY: a self-modifying system needs that.
It launches each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop/pulse.py, each as its own process (5.8.3.4).
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.

The ground loop finds one pulse.py per device. pulse.py reads its own device's declared instances (5.7.3.4) and pulses each one, so the ground loop never needs to know instances exist. Pulsing an instance that isn't connected is what starts its shim.
Any shim, through its pulse.py, brings the bus up if it's down: whatever is called brings up what it needs (5.3.4.1).

pulse.py asks nobody anything. It starts the shim if it's down, else tells the mechanisms inside the shim that need a pulse "here ya go!" Only daemon-shaped things hang there, things that actually need a heartbeat (eg cc's Gmail fetch, 10.3.6); everything else fires on events. WHY: pulse.py is a place to hang daemons from, not managers.

There is no central supervisor. Each part starts what it needs by trying to use it: sending a message starts the bus if it is down, a message arriving wakes its shim, the shim wakes its device. Many very small supervisors, each one detect-and-start. WHY: a supervisor is one more thing to keep up, and the system must come up from any part that is touched.
The detect-and-start lives in one tool, the waker, and it sits inside connect: every client's connect is a wake attempt, so no caller can forget one. A probe watches and reports; the waker acts.
Any cairn command brings up whatever it needs, including the whole install on the very first run (6.3.2). WHY: a well designed tool should disappear in use.

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.
